plan_a_advantages: Includes longer, more realistic trail running distances and durations.
Prioritizes building a strong aerobic base through consistent long runs.
Incorporates varied terrain in long runs and hill sessions, simulating trail conditions.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on developing threshold strength, which can be beneficial for climbing.
Includes a dedicated strength and mobility session, addressing a potentially overlooked area for trail runners.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates longer, more sustained efforts that directly translate to trail running performance. While Plan B focuses heavily on threshold work and strength, it lacks the crucial long runs and varied terrain sessions that are fundamental to building the endurance needed for trail races. Plan A’s emphasis on controlled long runs and consistent hill work will build a stronger aerobic base and improve the runner’s ability to handle the demands of a trail race, whereas Plan B’s shorter, more intense sessions could lead to burnout or overtraining without sufficient recovery and volume. Furthermore, the inclusion of a dedicated easy run at the end of the week is a key component for recovery and adaptation.
